title: FluencyCraft Intermediate - Day 03
concept_overview: Day 3: Team Collaboration, Deadline Adjustments & Bottlenecks
why_important: Negotiating deadlines constructively maintains productivity and team trust.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A point of congestion that delays progress in a process
word_of_the_day.usage: We identified a testing bottleneck that slowed down our deployment.

questions.question: Day 3 Practice: When talking about making morning tea (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'I'?

options.a: I am have fresh cup tea.
options.b: I am having a fresh cup of tea before leaving.
options.c: I is have fresh cup tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I am having a fresh cup of tea before leaving.".

questions.question: Day 3 Practice: When talking about tidying up the room (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

options.b: I am tidying up the room right now.

Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I am tidying up the room right now.".

questions.question: Day 3 Practice: When talking about rescheduling a team sync (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

questions.question: Day 3 Vocabulary: What is the exact practical meaning of the everyday phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: To stop doing all daily activities immediately.
options.b: Carefully choose specific items from a group.
options.c: To clean the room using water.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question: Day 3 Vocabulary: What is the exact practical meaning of the everyday phrase 'drop by'?

options.a: To stop doing all daily activities immediately.
options.b: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.c: To clean the room using water.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 3 Vocabulary: What is the exact practical meaning of the everyday phrase 'follow up'?

options.a: To stop doing all daily activities immediately.
options.b: Check progress on a prior matter.
options.c: To clean the room using water.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question: Day 3 Vocabulary: What is the exact practical meaning of the everyday phrase 'drop off'?

options.a: To stop doing all daily activities immediately.
options.b: Take someone to a destination and leave them there.
options.c: To clean the room using water.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'drop off' means: take someone to a destination and leave them there. Example: "Please drop me off near the bus stand."

questions.question:
Day 3 Translation Scenario 1:

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.

questions.explanation:
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 3 Translation Scenario 2:

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.b: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 3 Translation Scenario 3:

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.

questions.explanation:
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 3 Translation Scenario 4:

Telugu: "సాయంత్రం మా ఇంటికి రండి, టీ తాగుదాం."
(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: Evening my house come, tea drink.
options.b: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.

questions.explanation:
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.
